notes: Individual exact-identity review: Electro-Voice's official EVF/EVH User Manual (June 2010) defines the slash suffix in the model number as the coverage-pattern code and lists six distinct 15-inch EVF-1152D variants: /43, /64, /66, /94, /96, and /99, with rotatable coverage from 40° × 30° through 90° × 90°. Exact /43, /66, /94, and /96 Engineering Data Sheets publish variant-specific coverage, response tables, and 1/3-octave polar plots. The manufacturer also distinguishes PI and FG weatherization suffixes; the exact sheets state an externally accessible jumper selects passive or active operation. The database row is only 'EVF-1152D' and does not identify its pattern, environmental suffix, or operating configuration. No exact SKU/polar variant is established, so none of the pattern-specific response, sensitivity, impedance, power, driver, or directivity specifications is assigned. The catalog retains the exact EVF-1152D/96 as the separate record `electro-voice-evf-1152d-96`; its suffix-specific values are not transferred to this bare row. Review of all text-extractable chunks of the official /43, /66, /94, and /96 engineering sheets confirms their response-table and polar/beamwidth/directivity sections. However, the extracted /94 and /96 low-frequency rows include values inconsistent with the same sheets’ stated frequency-range limits (for example, /96 shows 80 dB at 44 Hz despite a 40 Hz -10 dB lower limit). This may be an extraction artifact; without reliable visual verification, no response points are digitized. The polar charts are not exposed as numeric angle-resolved samples in the text extraction, so no directivity payload is imported. The separate exact /96 record remains unchanged; no suffix-specific values are transferred to the unsuffixed row. Preserve the legitimate row with unsupported fields N/A and identity status UNAVAILABLE until the exact suffix/configuration is known.
